body:
Prima contains Eovar Harbor and the Thundering Coast, alongside Pristinia and the island’s inland landscapes. The island map above shows their relationship; the settlement maps offer closer views.

Prima compresses Fenumion’s whole argument into one island: an ancient Gate, a civilization destroyed by corrupted life, a new settlement above the wound, and a community attempting a different relationship with power.

Sublocations

Pristinia is the growing settlement where walls, farms, taverns, and food stores make history tangible. The Common Man was its accumulated civilian room; after zombie pirates burned it, Pilgrim’s Hearth inherited the same foundations. Protected record is the ancient mechanism that awakened when modern adventurers began arriving. Protected record is Melian’s ruined city, built above the Delerium vein that destroyed it.

The Before beneath the future

Melian’s people found Delerium, tried to use it, and were consumed from below. She urges learning as preparation rather than prohibiting knowledge. The Gate had been dormant since an age when gods walked openly; it awakened only when modern adventurers began arriving. Prima’s history includes ancient divine failure, mortals repeating destructive experiments, and later efforts to prepare differently.

The cost of saving Prima

Papirak’s public legacy joins ancient Gate-era participation to generations of teaching in Pristinia. His protected history is preserved separately; the public biography and funeral record follow the work inherited by the living.

Beyond the settlement

The Alpine Forest lies east of the Old Earth Hills. Modern fieldwork in The Before supplies a separate history of repeated exploration; the ruins’ ancient origins remain restricted.

An early traveler’s regional model

Scribonia’s location note posted on 8 March 2024, as recorded in his field note, attributes a simple regional model to the Master Librarian: Rahu roughly four or five days west of the Homestead, Kinnich Ahua roughly four or five days east. It records the guidance available to him then. Routes, conditions and means of travel are not specified well enough to turn these estimates into fixed map geometry.
